design: A hard bind with the numbers shown: a £43m hole, £8m of reserves and £5m a year from the highest council tax rise that needs no local vote. Closing the rest means selling council homes, cutting care, borrowing more or breaking the balanced-books rule, and each of those is a red line people will set. No answer can keep every limit without leaving the gap open.
tests_hint: Red lines citizens in that place would set: the books must balance this year and next (the bind itself); no council tenant loses their home or pays for the company's debt; no cut to adult social care or children's services; no council tax rise above the limit that needs a local vote; no new borrowing to cover the loss. Other tests: the 410 homes are finished or sold within two years; residents are told in plain words what was lost and who decided; the company stops making new loans. Numbers that keep it a bind: £43m gap minus £8m reserves leaves £35m; £5m a year in tax covers only about £15m in three years; selling 300 council homes would raise about £30m but means tenants lose homes.
angles: Sell council homes and sites to fill the gap
Cut services and raise tax to the limit over years
Wind the company down and ask government for help
